title: mailward classification rules
description: Named data the rules reference (refs: sender lists, regex patterns, age thresholds) plus the classify/cleanup rule arrays. Loaded by src/rules-data.ts.

classify.description: Unread-path rules, evaluated top-to-bottom; the first matching rule wins, no match → keep. Decides keep/markRead/delete.

cleanup.description: --cleanup prune rules for already-read mail, evaluated top-to-bottom; first match wins. Conservative: a protect rule (keep) should come first.

accounts.description: Per-account rule overrides, keyed by the account id from accounts.yaml. Each block deep-merges over the shared rules above (nested objects merge; arrays/scalars replace) — override e.g. one ref entry under refs, or replace the classify/cleanup arrays for that account.

refs.description: The named data rules point at via `ref: <bucket>.<name>` — sender lists, regex patterns and age thresholds.

lists.description: Sender-domain lists. Each entry is matched as an address SUFFIX (m.fromAddress.endsWith(entry)), so 'amazon.de' also matches 'no-reply@amazon.de'.

markReadDomains.description: Senders whose mail is legit but low-priority → marked read across all folders (never deleted). Newsletters and recurring FYI notifications.

spamDomains.description: Sender domains deleted when found in Junk. Throwaway spam hosts, plus brands the user has no account with (unsolicited).

protectSenders.description: Transactional/personal senders that --cleanup NEVER deletes, even when old (orders, invoices, receipts, forwarded personal mail). Overrides every prune rule.

promoSenders.description: Promotional senders whose time-limited offers are safe for --cleanup to prune once stale (older than thresholds.stalePromo, or with expiry language).

monthlySenders.description: 'Read-once' senders: actively read when fresh but worthless after ~a month. Marked read on arrival, then pruned by --cleanup once older than thresholds.monthly.

patterns.description: Named regular expressions. Each is compiled case-insensitively (the 'i' flag). Single-quote them in YAML so backslashes stay literal (write \b, not \\b).

spamSubject.description: Classic spam subjects (gambling, pharma, scam finance, fake alerts). Matched against the subject of Junk mail → delete.

phishing.description: Credential/account-update phishing lures. Matched against subject + body of Junk mail → delete.

moneyScam.description: Advance-fee / lottery money scams (large sums legit personal mail rarely carries). Matched against subject + body of Junk mail → delete.

emotionalScam.description: Romance / charity / emotional-manipulation bait. Matched against subject + body of Junk mail → delete.

impersonation.description: Brand-impersonation phishing & known scams (Apple/App Store, 'as seen on TV' offers, home warranty). Matched against the subject of Junk mail → delete.

fakeParcel.description: Fake parcel/delivery notifications. Matched against the subject of Junk mail → delete. (Real DHL/Amazon come from their own domains and never land in Junk.)

protectSubject.description: Subjects marking a message as transactional/important (invoice, order, booking, receipt …). --cleanup NEVER deletes a message whose subject matches.

digestSubject.description: Periodic, non-offer digests from promo senders (e.g. a weekly activity/performance report). Not time-limited offers → kept ~a month (thresholds.digest), not pruned at the 7-day promo cadence.

expiry.description: Explicit 'this offer expires / ends soon' language. From a promo sender it marks a stale offer for --cleanup to prune; also shown as the 'Expiry signal' column.

thresholds.description: Age thresholds as human-readable durations (parse-duration): '7d', '30 days', '1440 min', '36h' all work. Converted to hours internally.

stalePromo.description: A promotional mail older than this is pruned by --cleanup (promo-stale).

monthly.description: 'Read-once' mail (monthlySenders) older than this is pruned by --cleanup (monthly-stale).

digest.description: A periodic digest (digestSubject) from a promo sender older than this is pruned by --cleanup (promo-digest-old); younger ones are kept.

promoExpiredMin.description: Minimum age before an expiry-flagged promo is pruned, so an offer 'valid for 24h' that arrived today is only removed from tomorrow (promo-expired).

name.description: Short identifier, surfaced as the decision reason in the result table.

when.description: The condition that must hold for this rule to fire.

condition.description: A leaf test ({field, op, value|ref}) or a combinator (all / any / not).

all.description: Matches when ALL sub-conditions match (logical AND).

any.description: Matches when ANY sub-condition matches (logical OR).

not.description: Matches when the sub-condition does NOT match (logical NOT).

leaf.description: A single field test. Provide either `value` (inline literal) or `ref` (a refs entry, <bucket>.<name>).

field.description: Message field to test. `content` = subject + body; `folder` = the LEAF folder name (so 'GitHub' matches 'Archive/GitHub'); `age` = age in hours.

op.description: Comparison. String ops are case-insensitive except `equals` (exact). `regex` is case-insensitive. `endsWithAny` needs a list operand. `>`/`>=` need the numeric `age` field.

value.description: Inline literal operand (string, number, or list of strings for endsWithAny).

ref.description: A named entry under `refs:`, as `<bucket>.<name>` where <bucket> is one of refs' three buckets: lists.* (sender lists → endsWithAny), patterns.* (regexes → regex), or thresholds.* (ages in hours → '>' / '>='). E.g. 'lists.markReadDomains', 'patterns.spamSubject', 'thresholds.monthly'.
